shots.content: Inside a kitchen, a rectangular island stands between a sink counter and a refrigerator, with a window along one side and an aisle along the opposite side. A man in a green shirt sits on the sink-side window stool proposing a stew recipe, a woman in a white shirt sits on the sink-side aisle stool, and a woman in a blue shirt sits on the refrigerator-side aisle stool. There is one empty place.
shots.viewpoint: Wide establishing shot from just beside the refrigerator end, looking along the kitchen island toward the sink counter, with both window-side stools and both aisle-side stools and the sink counter in frame.

shots.content: A woman in an orange shirt enters and sits in the empty place. She asks about the vegetable peeling technique for the stew, and a man in a green shirt argues for scraping instead.
shots.viewpoint: Medium two-shot from the aisle side, centered on the two adjacent window-side stools.

shots.content: A man in a green shirt explains why scraping ingredients saves more of the vegetables.
shots.viewpoint: Close-up from the aisle side, centered on the person at the sink-side window stool.

shots.content: A woman in a blue shirt argues that scraping takes too much effort, and a man in a green shirt replies.
shots.viewpoint: Reverse wide shot of the kitchen island.
